Today we celebrate Indigenous Peoples' Day.

Native peoples have lived on, cared for, and shaped the land we now call Ohio for thousands of years. Their history, cultures, and contributions are part of our story, and they deserve to be honored, taught, and remembered, not just today but all year.

I'm grateful for the Native communities who continue to carry their traditions forward and enrich our state. Today is a chance to learn, listen, and reflect on that legacy together.

Today is World Mental Health Day.

Taking care of our mental health is just as important as taking care of our physical health, and no one should have to face a hard time alone. To everyone in Ohio's 13th District who is struggling, or who is supporting someone who is: you matter, and help is available.

If you or someone you know needs support, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, any time, day or night. Reaching out is a sign of strength.
Thank you to the counselors, nurses, social workers, and caregivers across our community who show up for their neighbors every day.

Big news for Akron! The University of Akron has received a $241,455 grant from the National Eye Institute to study how cells in the retina communicate. Vision research leads to better ways to understand, prevent, and treat eye disease, and it gives students hands-on experience that prepares them for careers in science and medicine. Northeast Ohio is home to researchers asking important questions, and I'm proud to support their work. #MoneyMonday

From Ohio’s 13th District to Arizona to Massachusetts to Minnesota, the headlines are the same: SNAP cuts are putting food out of reach for families. I voted against the Republican bill that made these disastrous cuts, and I'm cosponsoring legislation to repeal them. Families shouldn't go hungry in the richest country in the world.

The U.S. lost 15,000 farms in 2025, according to USDA, and Ohio lost about 400 of them. Only the largest operations grew, while small and mid-sized family farms are the ones being squeezed out. I voted against a Republican farm bill that fell short on support for farmers, and I opposed an agriculture funding bill that cut USDA staffing for farmer assistance programs. Our farmers feed us, and they deserve a Congress that fights for them.

94% of farmers say their finances are worse or haven’t improved this year. Trump's trade war has cost farmers their markets and their margins, and I'm pushing back against policies that put politics ahead of family-owned farms. https://t.co/NlOHL5sTkT

funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.
